title: Active voice
lede: Put the doer first. It's the single easiest way to make writing clearer and stronger.

sections.md:
## Active vs passive
- **Active:** the subject does the action. "Mike loaded the truck."
- **Passive:** the subject receives the action. "The truck was loaded by Mike."

Passive sentences are longer, weaker, and often hide who did what.

## How to spot passive voice
Look for a form of **be** (is, are, was, were, been, being) plus a past-tense verb (loaded, sent, made).

The zombie test: if you can add "by zombies" after the verb and it still makes sense, it's passive. "Mistakes were made (by zombies)." Passive.

sections.title: Flip it
sections.problem: "The payment was not received by our office."
steps: Who did the action? Our office (didn't receive).

sections.md:
## When passive is fine
Passive is useful when the doer is unknown or doesn't matter: "The road was closed for repairs." Use it on purpose, not by accident.

sections.label: Strong verbs
sections.md: Active voice pairs with strong verbs. Replace "made a decision" with "decided," "gave approval" with "approved," and "is in need of" with "needs."

options: The contract was signed by both parties.

practice.why: "Was missed" — missed by whom? (By zombies works.)

practice.q: Best rewrite of "A decision was made by the board to expand."
options: Expansion was decided by the board.
A decision to expand was made.

practice.q: When is passive voice a good choice?
options: When the doer is unknown or doesn't matter
practice.why: "My truck was stolen": you don't know who did it.
